text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Hearing aid company Oticon, which has changed its name to William Demant Holding, has bought U.S. company Phonic Ear Holding Inc for 230 million crowns.

--The tax ministry has won a court ruling that it need not repay 13 million crowns improperly collected from Monsanto-Searle on the import of weedkiller Roundup.The court ruled that Monsanto passed the surcharge on to customers and therfore could not claim a refund from the government.
--Trades unions and employers have both praised Denmark's role in the revised EU treaty and say that the next step should be to get east and central European countries in the EU as soon as possible.

--The Radical Liberals, coalition partners in the Danish government, are against Danish firms taking part in the international Joint Strike Fighter project. The Danish defence ministry fears it will miss opportunities to creat new jobs and gain valuable expertise.
--Receivers for Svendborg shipyard say that a buyer has been found, but will not say who.
--Eastern and northern European markets account for most of Danish export growth while it is slipping in Asia and South America.
--Finance Minister Mogens Lykketoft acknowledges that next year's rises in local authority taxes will hit the lower-paid, but he promises to get the rich in the next tax reform, in 1999.
